newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat says rate cuts won't hurt revenue.
newsitem.headline: Indosat says rate cuts won't hurt revenue.

text.p: Indonesia's international telecommunications provider Indosat said on Monday that recently proposed cuts in international telephone rates would have little effect on revenues.

Indosat said in a statement that the firm acknowledged Singapore Telecom's recent announcement to cut its international service collection rate by an average of around 7.6 percent starting from 1 January 1997.

"Traffic incoming and outgoing between Indonesia-Singapore currently is split 49 and 51 percent respectively, and the impact of the reduction of the accounting rate between Indonesia-Singapore will save 7.6 percent on our out-payment to Singapore Telecom," the statement said.
Indosat also said the Indonesia-Singapore traffic volume has grown 15 to 18 percent yearly.
"Combining these two situations together, we view that the effect of the accounting rate reduction to Indosat is more on the positve side for Indosat."

The company also said that a proposal by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to reduce Indonesia's current accounting rate to the U.S. to $1.30 per minute from January 1 against the current $1.40 would also have little effect.

"For Indosat, this new accounting rate will effect a reduction of 0.57 percent to our telephone revenues but as the traffic volume betwen Indonesia-USA is growing at 15-17 percent yearly, the total effect to Indosat's telephone revenues will not be too significant," the company said.
The company said traffic both ways between US-Indonesia in the first nine months of 1996 contributed around 13 percent of Indosat total traffic volume.
Indosat shares were down 175 rupiah to 6,300 in mid-morning trade in line with a fall in New York on Friday on reports of the rate cuts, brokers in Jakarta said.
